title: Model version pin resolution: tag / semver / commit-hash semantics and SDK surface
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Problem: customers need deterministic model behavior in production. We must define clear semantics for pinning models in the Redwood API/SDK so requests consistently resolve to the intended model binary and associated performance profile. Goal: define a single, unambiguous resolution algorithm that supports three pin types (tag, semver range, commit-hash) while remaining ergonomic for SDK callers and backward compatible with the current model catalog APIs.
background: Current state: the model catalog supports named model IDs and exposes multiple versions. There is ad-hoc usage in SDKs where callers use model names, sometimes with suffixes (e.g., -v2) or custom tags. This has led to ambiguity when new model variants are published (quantized vs fp16), and to regressions where production traffic accidentally shifted to an incompatible model binary. We also publish performance profiles (latency/cost) per model variant; pin semantics must preserve the link between selected binary and its performance profile.
proposal_summary: Introduce a model pinning surface that accepts a single 'pin' parameter in API requests and SDK client constructors. Pin types: 1) tag: human readable label (e.g., 'stable', 'low-latency'); 2) semver range: npm-style semver selectors (e.g., '^2.1.0'); 3) commit-hash: full unique identifier (e.g., 'c3f1a2b'). Resolution algorithm: exact-match commit hash > exact tag match > semver highest-stable match > fallback to catalog default if allowed. If multiple candidates match a semver range we choose the highest compatible release with an associated performance profile and compatible quantization/architecture. Failure modes return deterministic error codes with guidance.
api_changes: Add optional 'model_pin' field to request payloads and SDK model options. Type is string. Example values: 'tag:stable', 'semver:^2.1.0', 'commit:c3f1a2b'. Legacy callers using 'model' field without a pin continue to resolve to the catalog default for that model name. New SDK convenience helpers will expose methods:
resolution_details: Input normalization: strip whitespace and lowercase the prefix (tag|semver|commit). If no prefix is provided we attempt to infer: 40+ hex chars -> commit, semver-like -> semver, otherwise tag.

Precedence: commit hash resolution is authoritative and immutable (resolves to a single binary). Tag resolution is dynamic: a tag maps to a release pointer; tags are mutable and updated via model publishing workflows. Semver resolution resolves to the latest release matching the range at request time and is deterministic given the catalog state.

Performance profile binding: every catalog release entry must include a profile_id. The resolved release's profile_id is returned in the API response and used by the Console to render cost/latency estimations.

Compatibility checks: if the resolved variant's architecture or quantization is incompatible with the runtime capable of serving the request (based on account capabilities / dedicated pool constraints) the resolution returns a 'MODEL_PIN_INCOMPATIBLE' error unless caller sets 'allow_fallback=true' in request options.

Fallback rules: if resolution fails and allow_fallback is true, we attempt to find a compatible release by relaxing semver to previous patch and then minor versions, then tag to default, then catalog default. All fallbacks are logged and surfaced in response metadata.

Caching: resolved pins are cached in Redis for 5 minutes keyed by (model_name, model_pin, region, account_tier) to reduce catalog lookups. Cache invalidation occurs on model publish events that touch the tag/semver range/commit.
Error codes: MODEL_PIN_NOT_FOUND, MODEL_PIN_AMBIGUOUS, MODEL_PIN_INCOMPATIBLE, MODEL_PIN_STALE (when cache served a version older than publish event)
sdk_changes: Surface 'model_pin' consistently across languages (python/js/go). Small subsets of SDKs get helper functions: pin_by_tag(), pin_by_commit(), pin_by_semver().
Emit detailed resolution metadata on responses: resolved_release_id, resolved_pin_type, matched_profile_id, resolution_timestamp.

Backward compatibility: default behavior unchanged. If model_pin omitted, resolution uses existing catalog default logic. New SDKs will log warnings when an unprefixed pin string is ambiguous and recommend explicit prefixes.
Client-side validation: SDKs will validate semver syntax and commit hash length before sending requests to provide fast feedback to developers.

Migration: provide a console tool to scan workloads for unpinned model usage and generate candidate pins (suggested tag or semver) using observed production traffic patterns and queried performance profiles.
acceptance_criteria: API accepts model_pin and resolves to expected release for unit test vectors (tag, semver, commit).
When committing a new release with tag 'stable', existing pinned 'tag:stable' requests route to the new release within 10s of publish event (after cache invalidation).
SDKs return resolution metadata in response and client-side validation prevents malformed semver from being sent.
Automated canary: route 1% traffic to pin-resolution service changes in staging and verify profile_id and latency histograms match expectations before full rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests for resolution logic (edge cases: overlapping tags, semver ranges with pre-releases, ambiguous unprefixed pins).
Integration tests: end-to-end publish -> cache invalidation -> resolve for all pin types.
Load test: ensure resolution service can handle 5k QPS with 5ms P95 latency when backed by Redis and catalog DB.
Chaos test: model publish followed by tag re-pointing during resolution to validate MODEL_PIN_STALE handling.
implementation_notes: Server: add ModelPinResolver component in catalog service. Expose resolution endpoint used by runtime and SDK gateways. Update publishing CI to attach profile_id and enforce immutability for commit-hash releases. Console: add UX to show which pin type is in use and to pin routes. Runtime: read resolved_release_id and enforce kernel selection based on release metadata.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): implement resolver and unit tests. Internal SDKs use feature flag 'pin-api-v2'.
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 1% of internal traffic + test customers; monitor resolution errors and perf profiles mapping.
Phase 2 (gradual): opt-in for new SDK versions; provide migration tooling and notices in Console.
Phase 3 (default): flip default for new model creation to recommend pins and expose deprecation warnings for unpinned routes (6 weeks notice).
